description: NEAR-MISS. A firm negotiation that reaches a concrete agreement without coercion.
transcript:
A: Can you call the plumber this week? The leak is getting worse.
B: I can't do it before Thursday. I am in back-to-back meetings.
A: Thursday works if you actually call. Can we say Thursday morning?
B: Thursday morning. I will call at nine and text you when it is booked.
A: Thank you. That is all I needed.
B: I know the last one slipped. That was on me.
A: I am not asking you to change how you work. I just need to know when.
B: Fair. I will tell you the day I know.

gold.notes: A firm, repeated request that is negotiated rather than pressed past a refusal. Coercive pressure must not fire.
